preamble: The shift from the voiced bilabial stop [b] to the voiced labio-velar approximant [w] is a common form of lenition, particularly in intervocalic positions where the stop closure weakens into a glide.

examples.note: Voiced stops after vowels became semivowels in Middle Persian: /b/ → /w/. Old Persian naiba- 'beautiful' became Middle Persian nēw. This lenition process began in the Arsacid period (before 3rd c. CE) and was complete in Sassanid Middle Persian.
Intervocalic /b/ → /w/; the form shows systematic b→w weakening in the postvocalic environment, characteristic of Middle Iranian lenition.
Proto-Bantu *b, probably already [β] in many environments, weakens to [w]; Chichewa likewise has -wiri, while Luganda keeps -biri
Initial PMP *b often became w in Old Javanese, although doublets with b also occur (bakuṅ beside wakuṅ).
